skill.name: documentation
skill.description: Guides documentation work for TypeScript and React codebases, including TSDoc comments, Storybook stories, VitePress pages, and TypeDoc API generation.
skill.summary: Guides TSDoc, Storybook, VitePress, and TypeDoc documentation for TypeScript and React projects.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: All 28 static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline code, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. I found one contextual medium risk: the skill permits Bash and recommends running pnpm documentation scripts, which can execute project-controlled package scripts. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Project script execution without an explicit safety check
remediation.suggestion: Before running pnpm docs:api, docs:dev, docs:build, or storybook, inspect package scripts and ask for confirmation in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash access for documentation tasks
remediation.suggestion: State that shell commands should be limited to documentation tasks and should not process secrets or unreviewed scripts.

remediation.issue: Static analysis noise from Markdown backticks
remediation.suggestion: No security code change is required, but marketplace notes can clarify that these are Markdown examples, paths, and command references.

semantic_findings.title: Project Script Execution Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows Bash and recommends pnpm documentation and Storybook commands. These commands can execute project-controlled package scripts if used in an untrusted repository.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly allows Bash and documents pnpm commands, including a checklist item to run pnpm docs:api. The behavior is legitimate for documentation work but still creates execution risk in untrusted repositories.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss consistent API comments, component stories, and documentation updates. This skill guides TSDoc, Storybook, VitePress, and TypeDoc work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Adds TSDoc structure for exported functions, hooks, components, interfaces, and types.
Creates Storybook story patterns with metadata, default, loading, and error states.
Guides VitePress documentation placement under docs pages.
Lists TypeDoc API generation commands and expected output locations.
Provides a checklist for comments, stories, generated docs, and sidebar updates.
limitations: It does not include scripts or generators beyond instructions in SKILL.md.
It assumes a TypeScript, React, Storybook, VitePress, and TypeDoc project.
It cannot verify command safety without inspecting the target repository.
It provides documentation structure, not a full editorial review.

use_cases.title: Add Component Stories
use_cases.description: Create Storybook coverage for React components with default, loading, and error states.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Reference
use_cases.description: Add TSDoc comments and regenerate TypeDoc output for a TypeScript package.

use_cases.title: Organize Documentation Pages
use_cases.description: Place new VitePress pages and update sidebars when product documentation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic TSDoc
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for missing function comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add TSDoc comments to the exported functions in src/utils. Include parameters, returns, and one usage example for each.

prompt_templates.title: Document a React Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for hook API documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Document the exported hooks in src/hooks. Explain each option, returned state, returned actions, and common usage patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create Storybook Stories
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for component story coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Storybook stories for the components in src/components. Include default, loading, error, and important empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Documentation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for coordinated documentation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the public exports, Storybook coverage, VitePress pages, and TypeDoc setup. Propose a documentation plan and confirm before running project commands.

output: A concise component summary for the public API.
Parameter descriptions for visual state and click behavior.
Storybook coverage for default, loading, disabled, and error-related states.

output_examples.input: Prepare API docs for a utilities package.
output_examples.output: A TSDoc coverage plan, TypeDoc generation steps, and a review checklist for missing parameters and return descriptions.

output_examples.input: Add docs for a new VitePress page.
output_examples.output: A page outline, sidebar placement guidance, and cross-link suggestions for related API reference pages.

best_practices: Review package scripts before running documentation or Storybook commands.
Keep examples short and tied to real public APIs.
Update generated docs and source comments in the same change.
anti_patterns: Adding comments that repeat names without explaining behavior.
Creating stories without loading, error, and empty states.
Running project scripts in untrusted repositories without review.

faq.question: Does this skill write TSDoc comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides comments for exported functions, hooks, components, interfaces, and types.

faq.question: Does it support Storybook?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes story patterns for React components and common states.

faq.question: Can it update VitePress documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It points documentation pages to docs folders and reminds users to update sidebars.

faq.question: Can it run documentation commands?
faq.answer: It may suggest pnpm commands. Review package scripts and confirm before running them.

faq.question: Does it work for non-React projects?
faq.answer: It may help with TSDoc, but its Storybook guidance assumes React components.

faq.question: Does it generate TypeDoc output by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides the command and expected output location for projects that already use TypeDoc.
